fallback_summary_en: Languages divide meaning differently. Relationships such as purpose, reason, destination, recipient, exchange, and target time may use one form in one language and several forms in another. This lesson shows how the language you are learning handles them.

block_plan.notes: Show the generic support-language lesson blurb first. It must describe the semantic topic without assuming English, the support language, or the target language. It may also feed the lesson catalog and tooltip copy.

Universal intro in the learner's support/interface language: languages divide relationships such as purpose, reason, destination, recipient, exchange, and target time differently. Do not mention English or claim a one-word equivalent here.

After the universal intro, explain in the learner's support/interface language that English often bundles many of these relationships into the word 'for'. English is a comparison bridge, not the ontology.

Then personalize the lesson from the learner's support/native language using that language's reviewed forms/constructions when available. Explain how that language handles this semantic territory. Do not pretend it has one literal equivalent of English 'for'. When the support language is English, merge or omit this block to avoid repetition.

Explain the relevant grammatical category once in the interface language using selected-language form metadata. Do not call every form a preposition or conjunction; forms may be prepositions, postpositions, particles, case markers, clause markers, or larger constructions.
Localized explanation that one selected language may use a common form for several relationships that another language divides differently.
Render profile-preferred comparison bricks within the lesson-wide 2..6 language cap. Each brick may contain 1..N displayed forms.
Localized explanation that other languages divide the comparison territory across multiple forms/constructions and that every language owns its own rule boundaries.
For each selected lesson language, render one rule section per form and arbitrary rule/tip arrays from the grammar set. Never import another language's rule boundary.
Prefer exact approved handles from the current compatible text or the lesson-safe default corpus, including eligible Quotes Across the World anchors. Example resolution is content-owned.
Friendly localized transition such as 'Ready to try a few?' Omit when the selected direction has no meaningful choice to practice.

Use shared practice primitives only for selected languages with a meaningful practice decision. Wrong answers reveal the rule and rotate through reviewed rule tips; no punitive streak or harsh failure language.
Teacher/session policy may hide, offer, or require a reader quest. Omit the quest when the selected lesson direction has no meaningful target distinction.
Localized wrap-up and optional scorecard/celebration. Must also work for comparison-only sessions with no quiz score.

learning_path_policy.notes: The same multilingual lesson family may appear at different positions in different language paths. Spanish por/para may be relatively early, while Greek or another language may place the comparison only after its own prerequisites. Learner-tier languages may participate in the family without implying a full dedicated curriculum.
